passage:
Class 702 had a special homework assignment: spend no more than $100 in one week and write down every dollar spent.
Many students thought it would be easy. On Monday, they were careful. By Wednesday, some had already spent most of their money on drinks and snacks. By Friday, they began bringing water bottles and food from home.
At the end of the week, the teacher asked what they had learned. Andy said small things were not small if he bought them every day. Tina said she spent money when she was bored, not when she really needed something. Jack said he finally understood why his parents always checked prices before shopping.
The homework was not meant to make students love money. It was meant to help them see their choices. Money disappears quietly when people do not pay attention.
